columns/many: Multiplying two matrices is many matrix-vector products at once. A multiplies each column of B, and each answer becomes a column of the result.
columns/inner: So each column of B must be as long as a row of A: A's columns must equal B's rows. These are the inner dimensions, three and three.
columns/outer: The result keeps the outer ones: A's two rows, and B's four columns. Two by three, times three by four, gives two by four.
columns/rule: In general, m by n, times n by k, gives m by k. The inner n's must match, and they disappear.
order/swap: Order matters. B times A is three by four, times two by three: the inner dimensions are four and two, so there is no product.
order/batch: A common case: a batch X of N examples with D numbers each, and weights W with one row of D for each of C classes.
order/fix: X times W fails: its inner dimensions are D and C. Transpose W first: N by D, times D by C, gives N by C, a score for every example and class.
order/flip: W times X transpose works too, but lays the same scores out the other way: C by N.
